title: A single-point square-zero obstruction to versality
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work with $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal F$ be fibred in groupoids on their big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. A category fibred in groupoids assigns a groupoid $\mathcal F(T)$ to each scheme $T$ over the base, with pullback functors and coherent identity and composition isomorphisms. Assume also that for every diagram of base algebras $A\to B\leftarrow B'$ with $B'\to B$ surjective and square-zero kernel, restriction gives an equivalence $\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_B B'))\simeq\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)\times_{\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)}\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B')$, where the right side retains the specified isomorphism over $B$ and arrows compatible with it. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ be affine of finite type over $S$, and let $x\in\mathcal F(U)$. A point $u\in U$ is of finite type if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-residue-field]. For $x\in\mathcal F(U)$, versality at $u$ means: for every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local base algebras with common residue field identified with $\kappa(u)$ and nilpotent kernel, every map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and every $y'\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A')$ with a specified isomorphism $y'|_A\cong x|_A$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism $y'\cong x|_{A'}$ inducing the specified one. Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize; local means having a unique maximal ideal, and all maps respect the residue-field identifications. If $x$ is not versal at a finite type point $u$, there exist a commutative $\Lambda$-algebra $R$, a surjection $R\to R_0$ with square-zero kernel $I$, an object $y\in\mathcal F(T)$ for $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and an isomorphism $\theta:x\cong j^*y$, where $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ is the induced first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. The $R_0$-module $I$ is isomorphic to $\kappa(u)$. There is no open neighbourhood $W\subset T$ of $u$, no morphism $r:W\to U$ restricting on $U\cap W$ to the inclusion in $U$, and no isomorphism $\beta:y|_W\cong r^*x$ whose restriction to $U\cap W$ is $\theta^{-1}$. Equivalently there is no arrow $y|_W\to x$ whose composite with the restriction of $x\to y$ is the canonical restriction arrow to $x$.

source.place: Tag 0G2J (lemma-single-point), specialized to an affine Noetherian base; its affine pushout construction gives T=Spec R and kernel kappa(u).

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(u)$. Because $u$ is a finite type point, $k$ is a finitely generated $R_0$-algebra; adjoining its generators to finite $\Lambda$-algebra generators of $R_0$ shows that $k$ is of finite type over $\Lambda$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Negate the stated lifting definition of versality to obtain an unsolvable test problem. By [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra], its Artinian local surjection factors into finitely many small extensions in $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. If every small-extension problem at $u$ were solvable, start with the given map and specified isomorphism at the quotient ring and lift successively along this finite factorization, restricting the given object at each stage. Each new isomorphism extends the preceding one, so the final lift would solve the original problem. Hence there is an unsolvable small-extension problem $q:B\twoheadrightarrow A$, $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$, $z\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)$, and $\gamma:z|_A\cong a^*x$. Write $J=\ker q$. The definition of small extension gives $J\cong k$ and $\mathfrak m_BJ=0$, whence $J^2=0$ since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 0G2J (lemma-single-point), proof: small extension, affine pushout and contradiction

proof.text: Let $a^\#:R_0\to A$ correspond to $a$, and form the $\Lambda$-algebra $R=R_0\times_A B=\{(r,b):a^\#(r)=q(b)\}$ with coordinatewise operations. Its projection $p:R\to R_0$ is surjective: choose a preimage in $B$ of $a^\#(r)$ for each $r$. Its kernel is exactly $\{(0,j):j\in J\}$, whose products vanish. Thus $I=\ker p$ is $J$ as an abelian group. Multiplication by $(r,b)$ on this kernel is multiplication by the residue of $b$ in $k$, which is the residue of $r$ at $u$, because $a$ reduces to the specified point $u$. Consequently $I\cong k$ as an $R_0$-module. By the affine description of [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $j:\operatorname{Spec}R_0\hookrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a first order thickening. The projections give $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$ with $h|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}=ja$, by the contravariant description of affine morphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0G2J (lemma-single-point), proof: small extension, affine pushout and contradiction

proof.text: Apply the gluing equivalence assumed in the statement to $R_0\to A\leftarrow B$ and the triple $(x,z,\gamma)$. Essential surjectivity supplies $y\in\mathcal F(T)$ and isomorphisms $\theta:x\cong j^*y$ and $\delta:h^*y\cong z$ satisfying $\delta|_A\circ a^*\theta=\gamma^{-1}$. This is precisely an object mapping to the prescribed triple in the displayed fibre-product groupoid; no descent or pushout theorem is needed beyond that hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0G2J (lemma-single-point), proof: small extension, affine pushout and contradiction

proof.text: Suppose that $W,r,\beta$ as in the conclusion exist. By [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra], $\mathfrak m_B$ is nilpotent. Every prime contains all nilpotent elements, so the local ring $B$ has just the prime $\mathfrak m_B$. Its unique point maps under $h$ to $u$: the residue map $R\to B\to k$ is also $R\to R_0\to k$. Since $u\in W$, $h$ factors through $W$. Put $b=rh:\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$. The identity $rj|_{U\cap W}=\operatorname{id}$ gives $b|_A=a$. Pulling back $\beta$ along $h$ and composing with $\delta^{-1}$ gives $\eta:z\cong b^*x$. Its restriction is $\eta|_A=(a^*\theta)^{-1}\circ(\delta|_A)^{-1}=\gamma$, using the compatibility in the preceding step. Thus $(b,\eta)$ solves the small-extension problem, a contradiction. Finally an arrow $y|_W\to x$ over $r$ is, because the category is fibred in groupoids, the same as an isomorphism $y|_W\cong r^*x$; the composite-arrow identity is exactly the stated restriction identity for $\beta$. This proves also the equivalent formulation.
